title: Probe clears officers: TASER DEATH: Family believes there's been 'cover-up' from start
article: The family of a man who died after being Tasered by Vancouver police refuses to believe a report vindicating the officers involved.
Robert Bagnell, 44, was jolted with 50,000 volts of electricity in June 2004 while being subdued at a Granville Street hotel.
An external probe by Victoria police has found the Vancouver police officers acted properly.
"Your system of police complaints is a failure," said Bagnell's sister Patti Gillman, speaking Friday from Trenton, Ont. "It's police investigating police.
"I don't think police investigating police is ever going to work. And it's never going to give confidence to the complainant."
The 700-page report says Bagnell died from cardiac arrest due to a cocaine-induced psychosis. And it recommends better training and tracking of Taser usage, and the use of less severe restraints.
In a three-page letter to the family, Chief Const. Jamie Graham said "the appropriate amount of force was used to control Mr. Bagnell."

"It would be unlikely that the Taser contributed to Mr. Bagnell's death," he wrote. "The actions of the police officers were permitted in law and were consistent with their training and the policies of Vancouver Police Department."
Graham said he has accepted all the recommendations and is currently implementing them.
Gillman, who was given a 77-page summary of the report, now wants the B.C. Police Complaints Commission to hold a public hearing.
"We felt that there's been a cover-up from the get-go," she said.
Gillman said police waited a month before telling the family Robert had been Tasered, and then she learned they lost key data from the Taser guns.
"The VPD hasn't been able to say with any certainty which Tasers were used, when they were used, who used them, or for how long," she said.
The Bagnells' lawyer, Cameron Ward, also wants a coroner's inquest held, and a copy of the full report, including the autopsy and toxicology reports.
The complaints commission is now reviewing the report, and has the power to order a public hearing.
